reports.title: Laura-Jane Seaman: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: All Mid and South Essex Hospital NHS Foundation Trust ('MSE') sites have now adopted an electronic prescribing and medication administration (EPMA) platform. EPMA facilitates team members across specialties to record accurately and contemporaneously in one place. The system allows all registered users to clearly see what other medications have been administered and by whom. Staff details are visible against the record so that each interaction is name and date stamped within the patient record.
promises.summary: Adopt EPMA platform for medication charting

concerns.quote: The acute Trust 72-hour investigation did not identify: a. The absence of a contemporaneous Labour Ward medication chart for a patient that was administered medications on the ward
concerns.hazard: absence of contemporaneous Labour Ward medication chart

concerns.quote: Significant omissions in the medical record-keeping and some medications administered were entered into a medication chart from a previous admission in November 2023
concerns.hazard: significant omissions in medical record-keeping and incorrect medication chart entry

concerns.quote: Vital signs for patients on the labour ward being annotated on a piece of cardiotocograph paper and the absence of required MEOWS charts
concerns.hazard: vital signs recorded on cardiotocograph paper instead of MEOWS charts

concerns.quote: Communication issues with Trust staff and sharing of information
concerns.hazard: communication failures and information sharing problems

concerns.quote: Lack of compliance with national guidance and training
concerns.hazard: non-compliance with national guidance and training

concerns.quote: Absence of contemporaneous blood testing results for Laura-Jane as a patient at high risk of post-partum haemorrhage in labour taken at i. 00:40 hours for cross matching, and ii. urgent blood tests taken at approximately 04:45 for a deteriorating patient
concerns.hazard: absence of contemporaneous blood testing for high-risk postpartum hemorrhage patient

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems with communication and documentation within the Trust. The later report extends the concern to a trust‑wide, systemic issue rather than a single ward.
links.earlier_quote: d. Communication issues with Trust staff and sharing of information
links.later_quote: I am concerned that the documentation and communication failures identified in this case may not be confined to a single ward, clinical team or hospital site.
